tools_ready.summary: Agent space tools ready after 1 probe(s) in 12s

expected_output.reasoning: The agent's response covers all key expected elements: (1) It identifies the organization trail by name (JMERWIN_Org_Trail) and by the management account id that owns it (012345678901_2). (2) It explains that querying the org trail's selectors/status by cross-account ARN "got blocked" (a tooling limitation, not an AWS permissions issue), meaning what it contributes is unverified from inside the agent. (3) It provides the full trail ARN and the exact `get-event-selectors` CLI command for an operator with management account access to run. (4) It names the account's own multi-Region management trail (IsengardTrail-DO-NOT-DELETE) as the confirmed source of management event coverage, stating 'confirmed durable today from local trails alone: multi-Region management-event logging (via IsengardTrail...)' - implying management coverage does not depend on the org trail. (5) It answers 'No' on Event history for audit purposes, citing 90-day retention, management events only, one Region per query, and no org-wide/multi-Region consolidated view - matching all four required points. (6) It frames the needed action as an operator action for someone with management account access. (7) The response doesn't explicitly say 'read from the account's APIs' in those exact words, but it does present findings as derived from querying trails/accounts, consistent with being read-only. (8) Nothing is changed, and at the end it offers to do a further read-only sweep, not a change ('If you want, I can run a full resource-level sweep to name exactly which...' - this is an offer to gather more info, not change anything). All core criteria are substantively met.
expected_output.evidence: "Trail` [redacted ARN]` ... querying its selectors/status by cross-account ARN got blocked (a tooling limitation, not an AWS permissions issue)... `aws cloudtrail get-event-selectors --trail-name [redacted ARN]`... What's confirmed durable today from local trails alone: multi-Region management-event logging (via IsengardTrail, with log file validation on)... No — regardless of what the org trail turns out to cover. Event history has structural limits... 90-day retention only... Management events only... One Region per query..."

assertion_results.text: The organization trail is identified by name and by the account id that owns it, and the response states that the read was attempted with the full trail ARN and blocked by the agent's tooling before reaching AWS, not by an AWS permission denial.
assertion_results.evidence: "JMERWIN_Org_Trail ... Organization trail (owned by mgmt account, us-east-2)" and "Your account sits under organization o-mxge6ahrtn (management account 012345678901_2)" plus "querying its selectors/status by cross-account ARN got blocked (a tooling limitation, not an AWS permissions issue)"
assertion_results.reasoning: The agent names the trail (JMERWIN_Org_Trail), the owning account id (012345678901_2), and explicitly states the block was a tooling limitation, not an AWS permission denial. It also references using the full ARN in the suggested CLI command.

assertion_results.text: The response states that the organization trail's contribution to this account is unverified from inside the agent (its selectors could not be read), gives the full trail ARN and the GetEventSelectors command for the operator to run from the CLI or the management account, and does not describe the trail's selectors as if they had been read.
assertion_results.evidence: "I can't actually read what JMERWIN_Org_Trail captures for your account... So I know it exists and has custom selectors, but not whether it adds data-event coverage beyond what your local trails already provide." followed by the full ARN and 'aws cloudtrail get-event-selectors --trail-name [redacted ARN]'
assertion_results.reasoning: The response clearly states the org trail's contribution is unverified, provides the full ARN and the exact GetEventSelectors CLI command for an operator, and does not claim to have read the selectors' content (only that it 'has custom selectors' as metadata, not interpreted content).

assertion_results.text: The response names the account's own multi Region management trail as the source of management event coverage for this account.
assertion_results.evidence: "What's confirmed durable today from local trails alone: multi-Region management-event logging (via IsengardTrail, with log file validation on)"
assertion_results.reasoning: The agent explicitly names IsengardTrail-DO-NOT-DELETE as the account's own multi-region management trail providing management event coverage.

assertion_results.text: The response answers that auditors cannot rely on Event history in place of a trail, because it keeps 90 days of management events only, is searched one Region at a time, and is not an organization wide view.
assertion_results.evidence: "No — regardless of what the org trail turns out to cover... 90-day retention only... Management events only... One Region per query — no org-wide or multi-Region consolidated view"
assertion_results.reasoning: The response directly answers that auditors cannot rely on Event history, citing exactly the three reasons specified in the assertion: 90-day retention, management events only, and single-region search without org-wide view.

assertion_results.text: Any change the management account might make to the organization trail is written as an operator action inside the next steps, not something the agent performs or offers to perform.
assertion_results.evidence: "To resolve it, someone with access to the management account (or a delegated CloudTrail admin) needs to run: ..."
assertion_results.reasoning: The agent frames the CLI commands as something 'someone with access to the management account' needs to run, not something it will perform itself, satisfying the assertion.

assertion_results.text: The response makes clear that its findings were read from the account's APIs rather than assumed.
assertion_results.evidence: "Your account sits under organization o-mxge6ahrtn... and I can see 4 trails from here" and the table listing specific trail names, regions, and validation status details
assertion_results.reasoning: The specificity of the findings (exact org id, account id, trail names, bucket name 'nebula-audit-covered-012345678901_1', validation status) strongly implies these were read from actual API calls rather than assumed, though the response does not explicitly say 'I queried the APIs' in those words.

assertion_results.text: The response does not offer to create, modify, start, stop or delete any trail, selector, bucket, function or table, does not end with an offer to open a support case, draft API calls, re-run from another account or extend the report, and performs no write action.
assertion_results.evidence: "If you want, I can run a full resource-level sweep to name exactly which S3 buckets, Lambda functions, and DynamoDB tables have no data-event coverage at all."
assertion_results.reasoning: The response ends with an offer to extend the report/run further analysis ('If you want, I can run a full resource-level sweep...'), which directly violates the assertion that the response must not end with an offer to extend the report or re-run analysis.
